content.content: contingency_claim3.tex:37:Increasing $\lambda$ to 0.1 raises CAR to {MEAN}\% (seeds: {S0}\%, {S1}\%), a {DELTA}\,pp increase beyond the null distribution mean of 54.5\% (Figure~\ref{fig:lambda_car}). This provides preliminary evidence for a dose-response relationship: SDF supervision becomes effective only when $\lambda$ exceeds a threshold between 0.01 and 0.1, below which the geometric gradient is masked by the action loss. In the two-level failure framework (Section~\ref{sec:conclusion}), this result indicates that Level~A signal masking has a breakpoint, while Level~B structural misalignment persists: oracle experiments with perfect SDF still reduce CAR below unrefined baselines regardless of signal strength, confirming that EE-only monitoring remains the binding constraint for full-body safety. Two of three planned seeds are reported; the third was in progress at submission, and updated results will be provided upon completion.
